content.title: Celtics-Bucks recap: C's dominate offensively in 32-point win to close road trip
content.text: What to KnowChris Forsberg, Kayla Burton and Noa Dalzell shared more postgame reaction on the Celtics Talk Podcast.The Celtics (52-25) are 2.5 games ahead of the Knicks for second place in the Eastern Conference. New York beat Chicago tonight.The C's have won the season series vs. the Bucks 3-1.The Celtics now have an East-leading 26 road wins.Next up for the Celtics is a matchup against the Raptors at TD Garden on Sunday. The Boston Celtics are playing some of their best basketball of the season right now. They closed out their four-game road trip with a dominant 133-101 win over the Milwaukee Bucks at Fiserv Forum on Friday night. Jaylen Brown led the way with 26 points, while Jayson Tatum nearly had a triple-double with 23 points, 11 rebounds and nine assists. Neither Brown nor Tatum played in the fourth quarter. Six players for Boston scored in double-figures. The Celtics have scored 280 points over the last two games. They are on fire offensively. Check out our live blog below for a full recap of Celtics-Bucks: SCORE: 133-101 The Celtics are playing historically good basketball offensively right now. After scoring 147 points and hitting 21 3-pointers Wednesday against the Heat, the Celtics followed it up with a 133-101 win over the Bucks to close out their four-game road trip with a 3-1 record. Boston now has 10 wins by 25 or more points this season, and three of them have come against Milwaukee. Lots of players contributed to the Celtics' convincing victory. Six guys scored in double-figures, led by Jaylen Brown's 26 points. He was 10-for-11 from the free throw line. Jayson Tatum finished an assist shy of a triple-double with 23 points, 11 rebounds and nine assists. Neither Brown nor Tatum played in the fourth quarter due to the C's having a huge lead. Kayla Burton, Chris Forsberg, Eddie House, Drew Carter and Brian Scalabrine shared their key takeaways from the Celtics' 133-101 win during NBC Sports Boston's Celtics Postgame Live. Check out the segment in the video below: Neemias Queta scored 19 points with 10 rebounds (including the 1,000th of his career) and four blocks in the Celtics' blowout win over the Bucks. He talked about the team's recent offensive success and his own impressive performances during an exclusive postgame interview with NBC Sports Boston's Abby Chin. Check out the full interview in the video below: Abby Chin caught up with Neemias Queta after the Celtics blew out the Bucks Score: 105-76 Celtics The Celtics are absolutely dominating the Bucks, so it's fair to wonder how much run the starters will get in the final 12 minutes. Boston outscored Milwaukee 30-21 in the quarter. The C's have eclipsed the 100-point mark through three quarters for the second straight game. Jayson Tatum is an assist shy of a triple-double. He has 23 points with 11 rebounds and nine assists. Jaylen Brown leads the Celtics with 26 points. Five C's players in total have scored in double-figures. The Celtics are shooting 13-for-27 on 3-pointers. They increased their lead in the third quarter despite making only one 3-pointer in the frame. Score: 92-61 Celtics, 5:35 left in third quarter Jayson Tatum needs one more assist for a triple-double. He has 21 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists in 26 minutes of playing time. He now has eight double-doubles in 13 games this season. The Celtics are outscoring the Bucks 21-6 in this quarter. Score: 79-56 Celtics, 11:30 left in third quarter Jayson Tatum just made a 4-point play with a 3-pointer and a free throw. He's up to a team-high 17 points. The Celtics have outscored the Bucks 8-1 to start the second half, forcing Doc Rivers to call a timeout. Score: 75-55 Celtics Two nights after scoring 80 points in the first half, the Celtics dropped 75 on the Bucks in the first half Friday. The Celtics' offense is firing on all cylinders right now, and the 3-point shot has been a huge catalyst. Boston is shooting 55 percent (12-for-22) from 3-point range. Five Celtics players have made two or more 3-pointers. Five Celtics players have scored in double-figures, led by Neemias Queta's 15 points and team-high seven rebounds. Jayson Tatum is on his way to a triple-double with 14 points, a team-high eight assists and five rebounds. Jaylen Brown has 13 points, three rebounds and two steals. Payton Pritchard provided a spark off the bench with 12 points on 5-for-8 shooting in the second quarter. Score: 57-39 Celtics, 7:29 left in second quarter Payton Pritchard has scored 12 points on 5-for-6 shooting (2-for-3 on 3-pointers) in the second quarter. Score: 43-26 Celtics The Celtics scored 53 points in the first quarter against the Heat on Wednesday. The C's didn't quite match that in the opening 12 minutes versus the Bucks, but they still played well enough to earn a commanding 17-point lead. The 3-point shot has been the key to Boston's early success. The C's are 8-for-12 on 3-pointers, led by Sam Hauser, who has made all three of his attempts from beyond the arc. Celtics center Neemias Queta leads the team with 13 points, five rebounds and three blocks. Jayson Tatum is on early triple-double watch with nine points, five assists and three rebounds. Score: 22-6 Celtics, 7:32 left in first quarter Sam Hauser is back in his home state and he's on fire from beyond the arc. He's already 3-for-3 on 3-pointers. The Celtics, as a team, are 5-for-6 on 3-point shots. Score: 11-3 Celtics, 9:36 left in first quarter The Celtics already have an eight-point lead on 4-for-5 shooting (2-for-2 on 3-pointers) and four assists. Neemias Queta leads the C's with five points. The Celtics have won the opening tip and the game has begun. CELTICS Derrick White Jaylen Brown Sam Hauser Jayson Tatum Neemias Queta BUCKS A.J. Green Kyle Kuzma Ousmane Dieng Pete Nance Myles Turner The Bucks have struggled without two-time NBA MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo this season, to put it mildly. As a result, he will not meet the minimum games threshold for season awards or All-NBA teams. ESPN's Tim Bontemps does a couple MVP straw polls every season to see what experts think of the award race. The large majority of the people who participate in these polls have an actual vote for MVP. Bontemps released the results of his third and final 2025-26 straw poll Friday and Celtics guard Jaylen Brown placed fifth with 123 voting points, including one first-place vote. Here's the top five: 1. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, OKC: 958 voting points 2. Victor Wembanyama, SA: 644 Jaylen Brown joins Brian Scalabrine for an exclusive interview where they break down film and look at Brown’s growth into an MVP candidate. Jaylen Brown is in his 10th NBA season -- and he keeps getting better. The Boston Celtics star is averaging career highs across the board in points (28.8), rebounds (7.0), and assists (5.3) per game while improving his shooting percentage (47.6 percent) despite a higher volume of shots. With Jayson Tatum sidelined until early March, Brown has thrived in a lead role for Boston, emerging as a legitimate MVP candidate while helping the C's maintain a top-two seed in the Eastern Conference. Brown has dispelled plenty of narratives this season; he's been consistently strong driving to the basket with his left hand despite that part of his game previously being viewed as a weakness, and he ranks second on the Celtics in assists after being viewed as a more ball-dominant player earlier in his career. Brown recently sat down with NBC Sports Boston analyst and ex-Celtics champion Brian Scalabrine to watch film from his dominant 2025-26 season to date.
